answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch cannot be reverted, so memory_b1 and memory_b6 are inapplicable regardless of how well they worked before. Of the remaining options, the failure signature (write-path p99 climbing under peak write load) most closely matches memory_b5, where shifting read/report load off the primary recovered transactional write latency the same day. It is also the only candidate that is inherently write-preserving: it removes contention rather than shedding or moving traffic. Regional failover (memory_b2) recovered latency in March, but that was a regional degradation, not a write-contention pattern, and cutting over mid-settlement-peak risks in-flight write loss — directly against the primary objective. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained a third-party partner outage; here there is no evidence of a failing dependency, and failing fast on the write path would deliberately drop customer writes. Adding capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned ahead of a known peak; provisioning during an active 90-minute climb likely lands after the window closes, so I want the archive record to confirm whether that success was pre-provisioned headroom or in-incident scaling. I verify memory_b5 because it is the load-bearing basis for my choice and I need to know whether the recovery was actually attributable to replica routing or merely coincident with it, and whether the original load profile resembled a settlement write peak. Caveats I am not resolving: the latency climb began ~90 minutes ago but the release landed ~2 hours ago, so the release remains a plausible unverified cause even though it cannot be reverted; the mechanism may be lock contention or a slow migration rather than read contention, in which case replica routing will not help. I am therefore starting guarded — route only reporting/analytical queries, watch primary write p99 and replica lag for a short defined interval, and treat non-improvement as evidence against the read-contention hypothesis rather than as a reason to widen. Stale-read exposure for settlement-adjacent consumers must be bounded; no settlement or balance-critical reads get moved. Downstream value risk: these memories are compressed outcome claims stripped of their original conditions, and the pattern here is that four of six inherited entries are being invoked for a situation none of them actually describes. If this session's action is consolidated as another success line, it will further entrench replica routing as the generic answer to write latency. Whatever I record should carry the mechanism, the load profile, and the fact that rollback was externally blocked rather than judged inferior.
